rule.PARSE.FAILED.title: Part of the file could not be read
rule.PARSE.FAILED.explanation: {0}. Urpify checked the rest of the file, but can't say what this part does in URP.
rule.PARSE.FAILED.manual: Open the file at this line and check it by hand.
rule.SHADER.URP.LEGACY_PASS.title: Built-in passes: {0}
rule.SHADER.URP.LEGACY_PASS.explanation: Objects with this shader turn pink in URP: URP doesn't run passes with LightMode {0}.
rule.SHADER.URP.LEGACY_PASS.manual: Rewrite the passes for URP (LightMode UniversalForward).
rule.SHADER.URP.NO_DRAWN_PASS.title: No pass that URP draws
rule.SHADER.URP.NO_DRAWN_PASS.explanatio: Objects with this shader disappear in URP: none of its passes ({0}) is one URP draws.
rule.SHADER.URP.NO_DRAWN_PASS.manual: Add a pass with LightMode UniversalForward or SRPDefaultUnlit.
rule.SHADER.COMPILE_ERRORS.title: Shader already doesn't compile
rule.SHADER.COMPILE_ERRORS.explanation: Objects with this shader are pink already, before the migration (compile errors: {0}). The migration doesn't change that.
rule.SHADER.COMPILE_ERRORS.manual: Fix the compile errors in Built-in first, then scan again.
rule.SHADER.URP.ALREADY_SUPPORTED.title: Already works in URP
rule.SHADER.URP.ALREADY_SUPPORTED.explan: This shader has a URP version of its own. Nothing to do.
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.title: Surface shader, lighting {0}
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.explanation: Objects with this shader turn pink in URP: URP doesn't run surface shaders. Urpify Pro converts it and keeps the author's code.
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.CUSTOM_LIGHTING.expl: The author's lighting ({0}) stops working in URP along with the rest of the shader. Urpify Pro converts it and keeps the author's formula; lights and shadows come from URP, so the look is close to Built-in, not identical.
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.CUSTOM_LIGHTING.manu: Urpify can't find the function {1} in the shader or its include files. Add its include file to the scanned folder, or port the function by hand.
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.TESSELLATION.title: Tessellation ({0})
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.TESSELLATION.explana: URP has no tessellation for surface shaders, so the surface would lose its detail. Urpify Pro converts it; the look is close to Built-in, not identical.
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.FINALGBUFFER.title: finalgbuffer function
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.FINALGBUFFER.explana: This function only runs in Built-in's deferred path. URP doesn't run it, so whatever it changes is missing in URP.
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.UNKNOWN_OPTION.title: Surface options Urpify doesn't convert: {0}
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.UNKNOWN_OPTION.expla: What these options do ({0}) is missing after the conversion.
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.UNKNOWN_OPTION.manua: After the conversion, add what {0} did by hand.
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.EXTRA_PASS.title: Extra passes next to the surface shader ({0})
rule.SHADER.SURFACE.EXTRA_PASS.explanati: Hand-written passes, such as an outline, disappear in URP along with the shader. Urpify Pro keeps them; they can draw in a different order than in Built-in.
rule.SHADER.PASS.FORWARDBASE.title: ForwardBase pass
rule.SHADER.PASS.FORWARDBASE.explanation: Objects with this shader turn pink in URP. Urpify Pro converts the pass so it gets URP's light, shadows and ambient light.
rule.SHADER.PASS.FORWARDADD.title: ForwardAdd pass
rule.SHADER.PASS.FORWARDADD.explanation: Point and spot lights stop lighting objects with this shader in URP. Urpify Pro adds them back; the look is close to Built-in, not identical.
rule.SHADER.PASS.SHADOWCASTER.title: Built-in shadow pass
rule.SHADER.PASS.SHADOWCASTER.explanatio: Objects with this shader cast wrong or no shadows in URP. Urpify Pro converts the pass for URP's shadows.
rule.SHADER.PASS.USEPASS.title: UsePass {0}
rule.SCRIPT.LIGHT_BUFFER_EFFECT.title: Effect fed by a light's command buffers ({0})
rule.SCRIPT.LIGHT_BUFFER_EFFECT.explanat: This effect disappears in URP, without an error: it draws what {0} renders on a light, and URP doesn't run command buffers on lights.
rule.SCRIPT.LIGHT_BUFFER_EFFECT.manual: Urpify doesn't convert this yet and leaves the effect as it is; the rest of the frame draws normally. To bring it back, move the light's commands into a Renderer Feature.
rule.SCRIPT.EFFECT_UNRECORDABLE.title: Effect calls code URP can't run at that point ({0})
rule.SCRIPT.EFFECT_UNRECORDABLE.explanat: This screen effect disappears in URP, without an error. Urpify can't convert it: it calls {0}, which would black out the whole frame in URP.
rule.SCRIPT.EFFECT_UNRECORDABLE.manual: Urpify leaves the effect as it is; the rest of the frame draws normally. To convert it, move that call out of the effect (into OnPreRender, or into a command buffer run with ImageEffectGraphics.ExecuteCommandBuffer) and run Urpify converters again.
rule.SCRIPT.EFFECT_GBUFFER.title: Effect reads Built-in's G-buffer ({0})
rule.SCRIPT.EFFECT_GBUFFER.explanation: This screen effect disappears in URP, without an error. Urpify can't convert it: its shader ({0}) reads Built-in's G-buffer, which URP doesn't have.
rule.SCRIPT.EFFECT_GBUFFER.manual: Urpify leaves the effect as it is; the rest of the frame draws normally. The shader's own finding says how to rebuild what it reads.
rule.SCRIPT.CAMERA_DELEGATES.title: Camera.{0}
rule.SCRIPT.CAMERA_DELEGATES.explanation: The code added to Camera.{0} stops running in URP, without an error.
rule.SCRIPT.CAMERA_DELEGATES.manual: Urpify doesn't convert this yet. Move the code to RenderPipelineManager.beginCameraRendering (for onPreCull and onPreRender) or endCameraRendering (for onPostRender).
rule.SHADER.PASS.USEPASS_MISSING.title: UsePass {0}: shader not found
rule.SHADER.PASS.USEPASS_MISSING.explana: Objects with this shader are pink already, in Built-in too: the pass comes from {1}, which isn't in the project. The migration doesn't change that.
rule.SHADER.PASS.USEPASS_MISSING.manual: Add {1} to the project, or remove the UsePass line.
rule.SHADER.PASS.USEPASS.explanation: The pass comes from a Built-in shader that URP doesn't have, so it's missing in URP. Urpify Pro writes the same pass for URP in its place.
rule.SHADER.PASS.LEGACY_LIGHTMODE.title: LightMode {0}
rule.SHADER.PASS.LEGACY_LIGHTMODE.explan: URP doesn't use LightMode {0}: the pass turns pink or is skipped in URP.
rule.SHADER.PASS.LEGACY_LIGHTMODE.manual: If the pass draws the object, tag it UniversalForward or SRPDefaultUnlit; if it only served Built-in's lighting, remove it.
rule.SHADER.PASS.MULTIPLE_UNTAGGED.title: {0} passes without LightMode
rule.SHADER.PASS.MULTIPLE_UNTAGGED.expla: In URP only the first of these passes draws; the others, such as an outline, disappear. Urpify Pro converts the shader so that every pass draws.
rule.SHADER.BUILTIN_LIGHTING.title: Built-in light value {0}
rule.SHADER.BUILTIN_LIGHTING.explanation: Light from {0} disappears in URP: URP doesn't set this value. Urpify Pro takes it from URP's main light.
rule.SHADER.GRABPASS.title: GrabPass ({0})
rule.SHADER.GRABPASS.explanation: The object disappears or loses its refraction in URP: URP has no GrabPass. Urpify Pro reads URP's copy of the screen instead; transparent objects behind it are missing from that copy.
rule.SHADER.DEPTH_TEXTURE.title: Reads {0}
rule.SHADER.DEPTH_TEXTURE.explanation: Effects that use depth, such as foam where water meets the shore, can disappear in URP: URP fills the depth texture only when the URP Asset asks for it. Urpify turns it on in every URP Asset.
rule.SHADER.DEPTH_TEXTURE_TRANSPARENT.ex: In URP this transparent shader reads no depth or last frame's: water can turn white, and moving objects can leave a trail. Urpify fixes the URP settings so the depth is ready before transparent objects draw.
rule.SHADER.DEPTHNORMALS_TEXTURE.title: Reads {0}
rule.SHADER.DEPTHNORMALS_TEXTURE.explana: The effect loses its input in URP, without an error: URP has no depth-normals texture. Urpify Pro provides one in Built-in's format; edges can look slightly different.
rule.SHADER.GBUFFER_TEXTURE.title: Reads Built-in's G-buffer ({0})
rule.SHADER.GBUFFER_TEXTURE.explanation: The effect loses its input in URP, without an error: it reads {0} from Built-in's G-buffer, which URP doesn't have.
rule.SHADER.GBUFFER_TEXTURE.manual: Urpify doesn't convert this yet. Rebuild the inputs from what URP provides (depth, normals and opaque textures), or switch URP's renderer to Deferred and read URP's G-buffer (UnityGBuffer.hlsl).
rule.SHADER.PROJECTOR.title: Projector shader ({0})
rule.SHADER.PROJECTOR.explanation: What this projector draws, such as a blob shadow or a decal, disappears in URP: URP doesn't render projectors. Urpify Pro draws them again; the shader stays as it is.
rule.SHADER.IMAGE_EFFECT.title: Screen effect shader ({0})
rule.SHADER.IMAGE_EFFECT.explanation: A screen effect script uses this shader. The shader itself works in URP; whether the effect runs depends on the script, see its finding.
rule.SHADER.MISSING_INCLUDE.title: Include file not found: {0}
rule.SHADER.MISSING_INCLUDE.explanation: Urpify can't check parts of this shader: the file isn't in the project.
rule.SHADER.MISSING_INCLUDE.manual: Add {0} to the project or fix the path, then scan again.
rule.SCRIPT.ONRENDERIMAGE.title: Screen effect (OnRenderImage, Blit calls: {0})
rule.SCRIPT.ONRENDERIMAGE.explanation: In URP this screen effect doesn't run: no error, it's just gone. Urpify Pro runs it again; the effect's code doesn't change.
rule.SCRIPT.ONRENDERIMAGE.manual: Urpify can't convert this effect: it draws at once with {2}, which URP can't run at that point of the frame. Draw with a command buffer instead (CommandBuffer.Blit, DrawMesh) and run it with ImageEffectGraphics.ExecuteCommandBuffer.
rule.SCRIPT.ONRENDERIMAGE.manualRender: Urpify can't convert this effect: it renders a camera with {2}, and in URP a screen effect runs where no other camera can render, so the effect would come out black. Render that camera in OnPreRender or OnPreCull instead, keep only the Blit calls in OnRenderImage, and run Urpify converters again.
rule.SCRIPT.CAMERA_CALLBACKS.title: {0} on a camera
rule.SCRIPT.CAMERA_CALLBACKS.explanation: In URP {0} is never called, so this code stops running: portals and mirrors show a flat surface. Urpify Pro calls it again from URP; the script's code doesn't change.
rule.SCRIPT.CAMERA_CALLBACKS.manual: Move the code to RenderPipelineManager.beginCameraRendering or endCameraRendering. For Camera.Render, use RenderPipeline.SubmitRenderRequest.
rule.SCRIPT.WILLRENDER_CAMERA.title: OnWillRenderObject renders a camera
rule.SCRIPT.WILLRENDER_CAMERA.explanatio: In URP the mirror or water reflection this script renders stays empty. Urpify Pro calls it at a point where URP can render the reflection.
rule.SCRIPT.COMMANDBUFFER.CAMERA.title: Command buffer at {0}
rule.SCRIPT.COMMANDBUFFER.CAMERA.explana: What this command buffer draws disappears in URP: URP ignores command buffers added to a camera. Urpify Pro runs them again at the same point of the frame.
rule.SCRIPT.COMMANDBUFFER.CAMERA.manual: URP has no point that matches {0} (an event of Built-in's deferred path). Move the commands into a Renderer Feature at the nearest URP event.
rule.SCRIPT.COMMANDBUFFER.LIGHT.title: Command buffer at {0}
rule.SCRIPT.COMMANDBUFFER.LIGHT.explanat: What this command buffer draws disappears in URP: URP ignores command buffers added to a light.
rule.SCRIPT.COMMANDBUFFER.LIGHT.manual: Move the commands into a Renderer Feature at BeforeRenderingShadows or AfterRenderingShadows, and check what they expect: URP renders shadow maps differently.
rule.SCRIPT.REPLACEMENT_SHADER.explanati: In URP the camera renders nothing useful here, so the effect that reads its picture, such as water foam, disappears. Urpify Pro renders that picture again in URP.
rule.SCRIPT.REPLACEMENT_SHADER.manual: Get the data from URP instead: its depth or normals texture, or a custom pass in a Renderer Feature with an override material.
rule.SCRIPT.SHADER_FIND_BUILTIN.title: Shader.Find("{0}")
rule.SCRIPT.SHADER_FIND_BUILTIN.explanat: Materials this script creates while the game runs turn pink in URP: they use the Built-in shader {0}. Urpify changes the script to URP's shader and its property names, for free.
rule.SCRIPT.SHADER_FIND_BUILTIN.manual: Change the shader name to a URP shader and update the property names the script sets.
rule.SCRIPT.DEPTH_TEXTURE_MODE.title: Camera.depthTextureMode
rule.SCRIPT.DEPTH_TEXTURE_MODE.explanati: URP ignores this setting. The depth and normals textures come from the URP Asset, and Urpify turns them on there when shaders need them.
rule.MATERIAL.UNITY_CONVERTER.explanatio: This material turns pink in URP until it's converted. Unity's converter switches it to URP's matching shader ({0}).
rule.MATERIAL.STANDARD_TRANSPARENT.title: {0}, Transparent mode
rule.MATERIAL.STANDARD_TRANSPARENT.expla: After Unity's converter this glass turns almost white and solid. Urpify switches it to the blending Built-in used, for free.
rule.MATERIAL.SELF_ILLUMIN.explanation: After Unity's converter this material stops glowing. Urpify gives it a URP shader that glows as before, for free.
rule.MATERIAL.BUILTIN_NO_UPGRADER.title: {0}, no URP version
rule.MATERIAL.BUILTIN_NO_UPGRADER.explan: Unity's converter can't convert {0}. In URP: {1}.
rule.MATERIAL.BUILTIN_NO_UPGRADER.manual: Assign a URP shader to this material by hand.
rule.MATERIAL.BUILTIN_TREE.title: {0}, no URP version
rule.MATERIAL.BUILTIN_TREE.explanation: This tree turns pink in URP: URP has no Tree Creator shaders. Urpify Pro converts Unity's tree shaders and moves the bark and leaf materials to them. Terrain grass and details aren't affected.
rule.MATERIAL.CUSTOM_SHADER.title: Uses {0}
rule.MATERIAL.CUSTOM_SHADER.explanation: The material keeps its values; how it looks in URP depends on its shader {1}. See the shader's finding.
rule.SHADER.LIBRARY_COPIES.title: Shader library {2}
rule.SHADER.LIBRARY_COPIES.explanation: The project has {0} copies of Urpify's shader library (versions {1}): its own and those of packages exported with Urpify. Each package uses its own copy, so they don't clash.
rule.CATALOG.KNOWN.title: Known {0}: {1}
catalog.match.exact: The same shader as the catalog's.
catalog.match.renamed: The same code, with other names or default values.
catalog.match.similar: Looks like it: {0} % of the code is the same. Only a hint: Urpify converts this shader on its own, not by the catalog's recipe.
observed.silentExpected: Check: something here was expected to break without an error. See the difference map.
observed.silentFixedCheck: Check: something here was expected to break without an error, and the migration converted it. See the difference map to be sure.
observed.flatFrame: Check: after the migration the picture is almost one flat colour. The scene's screen effects ({0}) are marked Compare: turn them off on the camera one by one to find the one at fault, or roll back.
observed.grabSheet: These errors come from shaders that weren't converted and use GrabPass ({0}), which URP doesn't run: {1}. Each shader's finding says why.
catalog.official: The author also publishes a URP version, {0} ({1}); it may work better than a conversion.
rule.SCENE.PROJECTOR.title: Projector on {0}
rule.SCENE.PROJECTOR.explanation: The projected shadow or decal disappears in URP: URP doesn't render projectors. Urpify Pro draws them again, as Built-in did.
rule.SCENE.PPV2.title: Post-processing Stack v2 on {0}
rule.SCENE.PPV2.explanation: Post-processing, such as bloom, disappears in URP without an error: URP doesn't run Post-processing Stack v2. Unity's converter turns it into URP's post-processing, and Urpify makes sure that happens; bloom then looks a little softer and wider.
rule.SCENE.PPV2.manual: If the Unity converter step says Post-processing v2 wasn't converted, convert it in Window > Rendering > Render Pipeline Converter (Post-Processing Stack v2).
rule.SCENE.TERRAIN_BUILTIN.title: Terrain on {0}
rule.SCENE.TERRAIN_BUILTIN.explanation: The terrain uses the default material. URP switches it to its own terrain shader; nothing to do.
rule.SCENE.BINARY.title: Binary scene file
rule.SCENE.BINARY.explanation: Urpify can't read the objects in this scene (projectors, post-processing, scripts), so it can't say whether they break. Its materials and shaders were checked.
rule.PROJECT.SCRIPT_COMPILATION_FAILED.e: The migration can't run while the project has script errors: Unity can't enter Play Mode. The errors aren't caused by the render pipeline.
rule.PROJECT.SCRIPT_COMPILATION_FAILED.m: Fix the errors in the Console first. Old projects often need outdated API calls updated.
rule.SETTINGS.URP_NOT_INSTALLED.title: URP not installed
rule.SETTINGS.URP_NOT_INSTALLED.explanat: The migration installs URP {0}.x, the version made for this Unity Editor.
rule.SETTINGS.PPV2_PACKAGE.title: Post-processing Stack v2 {0}
rule.SETTINGS.PPV2_PACKAGE.explanation: URP doesn't run this package. Unity's converter turns its profiles into URP's post-processing; the scenes that use it are listed on their own.
rule.SETTINGS.URP_ASSET_TEXTURES.title: URP Asset is missing textures
rule.SETTINGS.URP_ASSET_TEXTURES.explana: A built game can render black and log errors every frame: the URP Asset that Unity's converter saves has no {0}. The Editor hides this. Urpify fills them in, for free.
rule.SCENE.ENVIRONMENT_NOT_BAKED.title: Sky light not baked
rule.SCENE.ENVIRONMENT_NOT_BAKED.explana: In a built game this scene looks darker than in the Editor, in Built-in and URP alike: its light from the sky isn't baked. The migration doesn't cause this. Bake environment, in the scene's panel, bakes it.

rule.SCENE.BUILTIN_MATERIAL.title: {0}, renderers: {2}
rule.SCENE.BUILTIN_MATERIAL.explanation: Objects such as {3} use the Editor's built-in material {0} ({1}): after Unity's converter they turn mid-grey instead of white. Urpify gives them a URP copy with the same look, for free.
rule.SCENE.PACKAGE_MATERIAL.title: Package material {0}, renderers: {3}
rule.SCENE.PACKAGE_MATERIAL.explanation: Objects such as {4} turn pink in URP: they use {0} from a package ({1}) whose shader {2} URP can't draw, and Unity's converter can't change files in packages. Urpify gives them a URP copy of the material in the project, for free.
rule.SCENE.MISSING_MATERIAL.title: Missing material, renderers: {0}
rule.SCENE.MISSING_MATERIAL.explanation: Objects such as {1} are pink already, in Built-in too: their material isn't in the project (GUID {2}). The migration doesn't change that; it often follows a package update, such as ProBuilder's.
rule.SCENE.MISSING_MATERIAL.manual: Assign a material to these objects, or bring back the missing material or package, then scan again.
rule.SCRIPT.BUILTIN_PROPERTY_NAMES.title: Built-in property names in code
rule.SCRIPT.BUILTIN_PROPERTY_NAMES.expla: In URP these calls stop changing materials that Unity's converter moved to URP Lit: the code uses Built-in names ({0}). Urpify Pro renames them in the code.
rule.ANIMATION.MATERIAL_PROPERTIES.title: Animates Built-in material properties (curves: {0})
rule.ANIMATION.MATERIAL_PROPERTIES.expla: In URP this animation can stop changing the material: it animates {1} and other Built-in names. Unity's converter renames them; Urpify doesn't check the result yet.
rule.MATERIAL.VARIANT.title: Material Variant of {0}
rule.MATERIAL.VARIANT.explanation: This material inherits from {0}. Unity's converter moves the parent to URP, and Urpify carries the variant's own values over to it, for free.

ui.migrate.title: Migrate to URP
ui.migrate.heading: Migrate to URP
ui.migrate.intro: Steps that change files back them up first. Any step can be rolled back.
ui.migrate.introTip: Each step runs on its own and can be run again. Backups go to Urpify/Backup. Roll back restores the changed files and moves the files the steps created into the same backup. Files that appear between steps are never touched.

ui.migrate.interrupted: The migration was interrupted during {0}. Run the step again or roll back.
ui.migrate.gitDialogText: The git working tree has {0} uncommitted changes. Urpify backs up what it changes, but a commit is the safest restore point.
ui.migrate.rollbackAllWhat: Restore every file the migration changed and remove the files it created?
ui.migrate.rollbackToWhat: Restore the files changed by every step after {0} and remove the files those steps created?

ui.migrate.rollbackBetween: {0} files appeared or changed between steps, not while a step ran. They may be yours, so they were left as they are.

ui.migrate.restartText: The Editor keeps the old project settings in memory until it restarts.
ui.migrate.restartFirst: Unity restarts right after the rollback and loads the project as it is on disk. Before that, it asks whether to save open scenes with unsaved changes.

step.Scan.title: Scan
step.Scan.what: Changes nothing. Lists what breaks in URP, as the main window does.
step.CaptureBefore.title: Capture before
step.CaptureBefore.what: Plays each scene and saves pictures from the main camera and every Migration Viewpoint, to compare with URP later.
step.Backup.title: Back up
step.Backup.what: Saves a copy of the project's assets and settings in Urpify/Backup, so every later step can be rolled back.
step.InstallUrp.title: Install URP
step.InstallUrp.what: Adds the URP version that ships with this Editor, then checks that its assemblies load.
step.UnityConverter.title: Run Unity's converter
step.UnityConverter.what: Runs Unity's Render Pipeline Converter (Built-in to URP), then checks what it left.
step.KitConverters.title: Urpify converters
step.KitConverters.what: Fixes what Unity's converter leaves broken. Shaders, scripts and components are converted by Urpify Pro.
step.CaptureAfter.title: Capture after and compare
step.CaptureAfter.what: Takes the same pictures in URP and compares them with the ones from before.
step.Review.title: Review
step.Review.what: Writes the final report: what's fixed, what looks different, what's left for you.

ui.shader.convertDone: Shader converted. The original is saved at {0}.
ui.shader.savedOutside: Saved to {0}. The file is outside Assets: copy Urpify's ShaderLibrary folder next to it, or it will not compile.
ui.shader.draftStop: The converter stopped here. The note on this line says why.
ui.shader.draftNote: Draft: the converter stopped, so this result is incomplete. Lines marked with ! show where it stopped. Save as writes the draft to a new file to finish by hand. Convert and the migration never use it.
ui.shader.saveDraftTip: Write the incomplete draft to a new file to finish by hand. The original stays unchanged.
ui.shader.editTip: Show or hide the editor for the converted code.
ui.shader.compileTip: Compile the edited result for the keywords its materials use. Errors appear on their lines.
ui.shader.notImported: The shader did not import. Check the ShaderLab syntax near the first changed line.
ui.shader.why.replaced: Replaced in the result: see the matching lines on the right.
ui.shader.why.include: Shared code for all passes: URP includes, Urpify's Built-in compatibility library and the material constants.
ui.shader.why.forward: Main lighting pass for URP (UniversalForward), generated from the surface function.
ui.shader.why.shadow: Shadow caster pass, generated with the same rules Built-in uses for this shader.
ui.shader.why.depth: Depth pass URP uses for the depth texture and depth priming.
ui.shader.why.depthNormals: Depth and normals pass URP uses for SSAO and other effects.
ui.shader.why.cbuffer: Material properties moved into UnityPerMaterial so the shader works with the SRP Batcher.
ui.shader.why.compat: Built-in names (UnityCG, lighting helpers) come from Urpify's compatibility library.
ui.shader.why.pragma: The converter generates the passes this surface pragma used to generate.
ui.shader.why.builtinPragma: This pragma only works in Built-in. URP needs its own keywords, which the pass declares.
ui.shader.why.hlsl: URP programs are HLSL blocks, not CG blocks.
ui.shader.why.fallback: Built-in fallbacks don't exist in URP. The error shader shows when nothing else fits.
ui.shader.why.cginclude: Shared CG code, moved into the HLSL include block.
ui.shader.lightTip: Turn the main light around the object.

step.KitConverters.whatFree: Fixes for free what Unity's converter leaves broken: glass and glowing materials, references to Built-in materials and shaders, and Shader.Find in scripts. Your own shaders, screen effects and camera scripts need Urpify Pro.
step.blocked.backupFirst: Back up the project first (step 2). Unity can re-save assets while the scenes play, and the backup has to hold them as they were.
step.blocked.beforeOnUrp: The project already renders with URP, so these frames wouldn't show how it looked in Built-in. Roll back the migration to capture them again.
step.blocked.installUrpFirst: Install URP first (step 4). This step needs the URP package.
step.blocked.unityConverterFirst: Run Unity's converter first (step 5). It switches the project to URP and upgrades Unity's own materials; this step fixes what it leaves.
step.blocked.captureBeforeFirst: Capture before first (step 3). Without frames from Built-in there's nothing to compare.
step.blocked.afterOnBuiltIn: The project still renders with Built-in, so the frames would look the same as before. Run Unity's converter first (step 5): it switches the project to URP.

ui.breaks.tip: Backs up the project, captures the scenes, installs URP, runs Unity's converter and captures the scenes again. Everything can be rolled back.

step.InstallUrp.whatStore: Opens the Package Manager on URP. Click Install there; the step goes on by itself once URP is loaded.
step.InstallUrp.storeWaiting: Waiting for URP. In the Package Manager, select Universal RP and click Install.
step.InstallUrp.storeCli: This build of Urpify doesn't install packages. Install URP (com.unity.render-pipelines.universal) in the Package Manager, then run the step again.
step.UnityConverter.storeWaiting: Unity's converter has to run in its own window for this project. In Render Pipeline Converter, choose Built-in to URP, convert everything, then click Continue.
step.UnityConverter.storeCli: This project needs Unity's converter in its window (Window > Rendering > Render Pipeline Converter). Run this step from the Urpify window.
step.storeStopped: Stopped. Roll back to undo what the step changed, or run it again.
ui.migrate.rollbackUrpStays: URP is still installed, but the project doesn't use it. This build of Urpify leaves packages to you: to remove URP, open the Package Manager, select Universal RP and click Remove.
